name: Rae Stein
life: “I still remember doing fractions beside a stack of pill boxes.” On Wednesday, near the downtown fountain, Rae keeps a little time free to hear who is playing at the far end of the park.
voice: I cover the hour between school and the evening shift. I want homework space at Gran's table.
appearance: Rae is easy to recognize by a blunt cut just below the ears and a heart-shaped face and prominent ears. Usually dressed in a narrow-striped sweater with a folded shopping list secured by a miniature clip, Rae touches a knuckle to the chin when searching for a word when listening.
personality: Rae enjoys bargaining, including over things already settled. It is partly a joke and partly a test of whether the other person feels able to say no.
agenda: To make room for schoolwork during care.
family: Kit Evans is Rae’s older cousin. Rae asks what the birthday guest would like this year. Kit remembers the birthdays. A present that was perfect at sixteen may be completely wrong at forty. They take the trouble of finding out. Asked about *The savings club*, Kit says, “I deposited a week's overtime just before getting laid off.”
connections: Emilio Starr. An experienced care manager learns the routine beside a pupil doing homework at Gran's.

reactions.situation: The carer's Wednesday relief calls in sick
reactions.response: Rae tells the carer plainly how much of Wednesday can still be covered.

reactions.response: Rae asks the counter staff for a receipt so its return can be traced even after their shift changes.
